note.text: Before German annexation, the territory now called Cameroon contained diverse political communities, economies and belief systems. Some communities had central rulers and courts; others distributed authority among councils, lineage heads or associations. Farming, craft production and local and long-distance exchange supported livelihoods. Coastal intermediaries connected inland producers with overseas commerce. These societies changed over time and should not be described as one identical political system or as having no history before Europeans arrived.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: Before German annexation, the territory now called Cameroon contained diverse political communities, economies and belief systems. Some communities had central rulers and courts; others distributed authority among councils, lineage heads or associations. Farming, craft production and local and long-distance exchange supported livelihoods. Coastal intermediaries connected inland producers with overseas commerce. These societies changed over time and should not be described as one identical political system or as having no history before Europeans arrived.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: A class can compare a Grassfields kingdom's institutions with coastal Duala trading networks without claiming that either represented every community. A market exchange, a court decision and a lineage obligation concern different parts of social life. Today's national borders should not simply be projected backwards as the boundaries of a single precolonial state.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Ask which community, period and source are being described. Compare authority, production and social relations separately. Treat an oral account or archaeological object as evidence to examine, not as inferior merely because it is not a European written record. Avoid generalising one case to all Cameroon.
